correctness.rationale: For the displayed nine-point poset \(R\), independent enumeration in this audit checked all \(4^9\) assignments against the source and target order relations and found exactly 172 monotone maps. The actual beat-sequence certificate blob was independently replayed from scratch against the changing active mapping poset: all 168 deletions satisfy the required up- or down-beat witness condition, with 68 up deletions and 100 down deletions, and the surviving maps are exactly the four constant maps. Their induced order is the four-point circle. The order-dual source has the same mapping poset up to the target order-reversing involution, so the conclusion holds for both Cianci--Ottina spaces. Beat-point deletion is a strong deformation retraction, proving the mapping-space homotopy type.

originality.rationale: Cianci--Ottina classify exactly two nine-point weakly contractible noncontractible finite spaces but do not compute their circle-valued mapping posets. Standard Stong/Barmak finite-space theory says beat points produce strong deformation retracts but does not determine which points are beat points in this 172-element function poset. Resultary searches found several other exact finite mapping-space computations at the same snapshot, including different domains such as the canonical finite spheres and projective plane, but no earlier source covering these two nine-point spaces. The exact 172-map enumeration and complete beat collapse are therefore additional same-object information.

value.rationale: The two nine-point spaces are the canonical minimal examples separating weak contractibility from finite-space contractibility, and the four-point circle is the canonical minimal \(S^1\) model. Showing that every individual map is nullhomotopic while the full finite mapping space retains a circle core exposes a natural and nontrivial exponentiation phenomenon in finite homotopy theory.

final_claim: For each of the two minimal nine-point weakly contractible but noncontractible finite \(T_0\)-spaces \(X\) of Cianci--Ottina and the four-point minimal finite circle \(C\), the pointwise mapping space \(\operatorname{Map}(X,C)\) has exactly \(172\) maps and strongly deformation retracts onto its four constant maps; consequently its Stong core is \(C\) and \(\operatorname{Map}(X,C)\simeq C\), even though all maps \(X\to C\) lie in one homotopy class.
limitations: The result is for the two nine-point minimal weakly contractible noncontractible spaces and the four-point finite circle target.
It concerns the finite pointwise/compact-open mapping poset, not the classical compact-open mapping space of arbitrary CW models.
